policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'from him who is and who was and who is to come' has no 'God'; the RP addition θεοῦ would require it.
ASV main text 'loosed us from our sins' renders λύσαντι; its explicit textual note says that other authorities read 'washed'.
ASV 'from our sins' does not distinguish ἐκ from ἀπό, and the textual note concerns the preceding verb rather than this preposition.
ASV 'for ever and ever' and its note 'Greek unto the ages of the ages. Many ancient authorities omit of the ages' explicitly support retaining τῶν αἰώνων.
ASV 'partaker with you' can render either συγκοινωνός or κοινωνός without distinguishing the prefixed form.
ASV has 'in Jesus', not 'in Christ Jesus', so it excludes the RP addition Χριστῷ.
ASV 'because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus' permits one διὰ to scope over both coordinated objects or a repeated διὰ before the second.
ASV has 'the testimony of Jesus', not 'of Jesus Christ', excluding the addition Χριστοῦ.
The readings differ only in the order of 'behind me' and 'a voice'; ASV word order cannot identify the Greek order.
ASV 'And I turned to see the voice' has no adverb 'there', excluding the RP addition ἐκεῖ.
ASV verse 13 says 'in the midst of the candlesticks' without repeating 'seven', excluding the addition ἑπτὰ.
ASV 'one like unto a son of man' does not preserve the accusative-versus-dative case distinction.
ASV 'as if it had been refined in a furnace' does not preserve the candidates' differing participial agreement.
The candidates differ only in the order of χειρί and αὐτοῦ; ASV 'in his right hand' does not identify the Greek order.
ASV ends the clause 'for evermore' without a following 'Amen', excluding the RP addition ἀμήν.
ASV 'the things which shall come to pass hereafter' renders γίνεσθαι and γενέσθαι alike.
ASV 'the seven stars which thou sawest' makes the relative the direct object of 'sawest', supporting accusative οὓς rather than genitive ὧν.
